column1: # user-scripts.tsv: Upstream's per-user setup scripts and whether Motanka's
# per-user setup runs them (design.md, "Per-user setup", step 4). Installed
# One line per script that Upstream's install/user/all.sh runs at the pin,
# in the same order, fields separated by tabs:
# <script> is relative to the vendored tree. The motanka-core build fails
# when all.sh names a script that has no line here.
# A "run" script also has to pass the Call_Inventory at run time
# user-setup skips it, with a journal entry, when the inventory has an
# arch-tool, arch-path, privileged or user-unit finding for it, or a
# home-write finding outside the Namespaced_Paths (such a write would be an
# unplanned home-folder change, 6.4). "skip" also covers writes the
# inventory cannot see, such as paths built in variables or by programs
# outside Upstream. A "skip" script may still run elsewhere; its reason

column3: runs in the session instead, once per user after per-user setup, through motanka-default-theme.service (/opt/motanka/libexec/motanka/default-theme): omarchy-theme-set needs the running desktop shell; its Pi and Fcitx5 activations go through Motanka's overrides, and the session capture records its writes
writes native messaging host manifests into twelve browser profile folders under ~/.config, which other sessions use
writes ~/.XCompose, which GTK and X programs read in every session
reads /etc/omarchy/language, which Ubuntu does not have; omarchy-language seed calls sudo and writes ~/.config/uwsm/env.d
default/input-methods/configure.py --seed writes fcitx5 and environment files that the inventory cannot see
writes ~/.config/wireplumber and ~/.local/state/wireplumber, which every session of the user shares
runs alsactl store through sudo, which changes system state
changes the audio card profile, which wireplumber stores for every session
omarchy-display-text-size rewrites terminal configs and GNOME settings
appends to ~/.config/hypr/looknfeel.lua after per-user setup wrote it, so the ledgered file would count as edited by the user
in a virtual machine copies two Upstream toggles into ~/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr (namespaced)
creates a default keyring in ~/.local/share/keyrings, which GNOME and KDE also use
mise reshim writes shims under ~/.local/share/mise, outside the Namespaced_Paths
runs omarchy-lifecycle-dispatch setup-user, a no-op on Ubuntu amd64 through Motanka's override
